Energy Calibration Tutorial

This tutorial calibrates the energy scale of a germanium detector from a simulated Th-228 calibration spectrum. It follows the steps of the energy calibration in the LEGEND data production: a coarse calibration constant is found from the most prominent peak, the charge-trapping correction is fitted, every calibration line is fitted, and the fitted line positions and widths are used to fit a calibration curve and a resolution curve.

The data are generated in the tutorial and mimic the output of a pulse-shape analysis: an uncalibrated energy in arbitrary units of the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and a drift-time-like parameter qdrift. The results are therefore not tied to any real detector.

using LegendSpecFits
using CairoMakie, LegendMakie
using Distributions
using Measurements: value as mvalue, uncertainty as muncert
using Random
using Unitful
using Unitful: keV  # the function strings of the results refer to `keV`

CairoMakie.activate!(type = "png")

Synthetic Data

The spectrum of each calibration line is sampled from the peak shape model that is also used to fit the lines (see Peak Shapes and Likelihoods): a Gaussian with a low-energy tail on top of a flat background and a Compton step. The sampling inverts the cumulative distribution function of the model on a fine energy grid. The tutorial uses a fixed seed, so the numbers shown below are reproducible.

Random.seed!(1234)

f_peak = LegendSpecFits.get_th228_fit_functions().gamma_def

# Peak shape parameters of every line; σ² grows linearly with the energy
th228_lines = [583.191, 727.330, 860.564, 1592.513, 1620.50, 2103.512, 2614.511]u"keV"
shape_pars = [
    (σ = 0.73, n = 1865.5, step_amplitude = 3.0,  skew_fraction = 0.02, skew_width = 0.003, background = 3),
    (σ = 0.78, n = 452.9,  step_amplitude = 1.0,  skew_fraction = 0.01, skew_width = 0.003, background = 3),
    (σ = 0.83, n = 355.8,  step_amplitude = 0.5,  skew_fraction = 0.01, skew_width = 0.003, background = 3),
    (σ = 1.02, n = 206.8,  step_amplitude = 0.1,  skew_fraction = 0.01, skew_width = 0.003, background = 2),
    (σ = 1.04, n = 130.3,  step_amplitude = 0.1,  skew_fraction = 0.01, skew_width = 0.003, background = 2),
    (σ = 1.14, n = 385.1,  step_amplitude = 0.1,  skew_fraction = 0.01, skew_width = 0.003, background = 2),
    (σ = 1.25, n = 3130.4, step_amplitude = 0.1,  skew_fraction = 0.02, skew_width = 0.003, background = 1),
]

function sample_line(μ, pars; n_events, half_width = 60.0, n_grid = 10_000)
    x = range(μ - half_width, μ + half_width, length = n_grid)
    cdf = cumsum(f_peak.(x, Ref((; μ, pars...))))
    cdf ./= last(cdf)
    u = rand(n_events)
    # linear interpolation of the inverse cumulative distribution function
    map(u) do ui
        i = clamp(searchsortedfirst(cdf, ui), 2, n_grid)
        x[i-1] + (ui - cdf[i-1]) / (cdf[i] - cdf[i-1]) * step(x)
    end
end

# The relative peak heights follow the model heights; each line gets its share of 200_000 events
peak_heights = map(zip(th228_lines, shape_pars)) do (μ, pars)
    maximum(f_peak.(range(ustrip(μ) - 60, ustrip(μ) + 60, length = 2000), Ref((; μ = ustrip(μ), pars...))))
end
n_events = round.(Int, 200_000 .* peak_heights ./ sum(peak_heights))
e_lines = reduce(vcat, [sample_line(ustrip(μ), pars; n_events = n) for (μ, pars, n) in zip(th228_lines, shape_pars, n_events)])
length(e_lines)
200000

A flat continuum below 2614.5 keV and the drift-time-like parameter complete the data set. The energy reconstruction loses a part of the charge that depends on qdrift. The simulated loss is independent of the energy, so the correction fitted at one peak applies to all peaks. The conversion factor from keV to ADC units is arbitrary.

c_true = 0.01u"keV"            # keV per ADC unit
n_continuum = 150_000
e_continuum = rand(truncated(Exponential(700.0), 100.0, 2614.5), n_continuum)

e_true = vcat(e_lines, e_continuum)
qdrift = rand(Normal(1000.0, 300.0), length(e_true))
e_uncal = @. e_true / ustrip(c_true) - 0.5 * (qdrift - 1000.0)
length(e_uncal)
350000

Configuration

The calibration is controlled by a few settings per detector. They are the energies of the calibration lines, the sizes of the energy window around each line that is cut out for the fits, the peak shape used for each line, and the orders of the polynomials of the calibration and resolution curves. The values below are the defaults for a Th-228 source. The names Tl208DEP and Tl208SEP denote the double escape peak (DEP) and single escape peak (SEP) of the 2614.5 keV gamma line of Tl-208, and Bi212FEP denotes a full-energy peak of Bi-212.

th228_names = [:Tl208a, :Bi212a, :Tl208b, :Tl208DEP, :Bi212FEP, :Tl208SEP, :Tl208FEP]
left_window_sizes  = [25, 25, 25, 25, 15, 25, 35]u"keV"
right_window_sizes = [25, 25, 25, 15, 25, 25, 30]u"keV"
fit_funcs = fill(:gamma_def, length(th228_names))
binning_peak_window = 4u"keV"      # energy range around a peak used to choose the histogram bin width
quantile_perc = 0.91               # fraction of events below the 2614.5 keV peak
cal_pol_order = 1
fwhm_pol_order = 1
excluded_peaks = [:Tl208DEP, :Tl208SEP]  # escape peaks are not used for the calibration and resolution curves

th228_lines_dict = Dict(th228_names .=> th228_lines)
Dict{Symbol, Unitful.Quantity{Float64, 𝐋^2 𝐌 𝐓^-2, Unitful.FreeUnits{(keV,), 𝐋^2 𝐌 𝐓^-2, nothing}}} with 7 entries:
  :Tl208FEP => 2614.51 keV
  :Tl208b   => 860.564 keV
  :Tl208SEP => 2103.51 keV
  :Bi212FEP => 1620.5 keV
  :Tl208DEP => 1592.51 keV
  :Tl208a   => 583.191 keV
  :Bi212a   => 727.33 keV

First Calibration Constant

simple_calibration finds the 2614.5 keV full-energy peak in the uncalibrated spectrum. It returns a calibration constant c that converts ADC units to keV and, for each calibration line, a histogram and start values for the peak fit. The peak finder does not work reliably for a spectrum with few events per bin, so the position of the peak is given as the quantile quantile_perc of the energy distribution. The constant is only an approximation, since it ignores any offset.

result_simple, report_simple = simple_calibration(
    e_uncal, th228_lines, left_window_sizes, right_window_sizes;
    calib_type = :th228, binning_peak_window, quantile_perc
)
m_cal_simple = result_simple.c
0.009998736880387127 keV

The report is plotted with lplot, which is provided by LegendMakie. The keyword watermark = false removes the logo and date that LegendMakie adds by default.

lplot(report_simple, cal = true, title = "Simple Calibration", watermark = false)

Correcting Charge Trapping

ctc_energy fits a correction of the form e + fct * qdrift at the 2614.5 keV peak. The coefficient fct is chosen such that the peak becomes narrow and high. The function takes the energy in keV, so the uncalibrated energy is multiplied by the simple calibration constant. The expression e_expression names the uncalibrated energy in the function string of the result. See Charge-Trapping Correction for details.

result_ctc, report_ctc = ctc_energy(
    e_uncal .* m_cal_simple, qdrift, 2614.511u"keV", (35u"keV", 30u"keV"), m_cal_simple;
    e_expression = "e_uncal", pol_order = 1
)
result_ctc.converged || error("The charge-trapping correction did not converge")
result_ctc.func
"e_uncal + 0.47616996718483623 * qdrift^1"

The correction factor is given in ADC units per unit of qdrift. The simulated loss of 0.5 ADC units per unit of qdrift is recovered, and the width of the peak decreases.

(fct = only(result_ctc.fct), fwhm_before = mvalue(result_ctc.fwhm_before), fwhm_after = mvalue(result_ctc.fwhm_after))
(fct = 0.47616996718483623, fwhm_before = 4.6234920289912225 keV, fwhm_after = 2.939820396666164 keV)
lplot(report_ctc, figsize = (600, 600), title = "Charge-Trapping Correction", watermark = false)

The function string of the result describes how to apply the correction to a table of outputs of the digital signal processing (DSP). In the production dataflow, it is evaluated for every row of the table with ljl_propfunc from LegendDataManagement. Here the correction is applied directly.

e_uncal_ctc = e_uncal .+ only(result_ctc.fct) .* qdrift;

Simple Calibration After the Correction

The corrected energies are calibrated again. The result contains the histograms and the start values of the peak fits for all calibration lines.

result_simple, report_simple = simple_calibration(
    e_uncal_ctc, th228_lines, left_window_sizes, right_window_sizes;
    calib_type = :th228, binning_peak_window, quantile_perc
)
m_cal_simple = result_simple.c

lplot(report_simple, cal = true, title = "Simple Calibration After Correction", watermark = false)

Fitting the Calibration Lines

fit_peaks fits the peak shape of each calibration line to the histograms. The default shape :gamma_def is a Gaussian with a low-energy tail on top of a flat background and a Compton step. The shapes :gamma_tails and :gamma_tails_bckFlat add a high-energy tail and remove the step, respectively. See Peak Shapes and Likelihoods for all shapes.

With e_unit and m_cal_simple, the fitted positions and widths are returned in ADC units, because the calibration curve is fitted against ADC values. The results are dictionaries with the line names as keys.

result_fit, report_fit = fit_peaks(
    result_simple.peakhists, result_simple.peakstats, th228_names;
    e_unit = result_simple.unit, calib_type = :th228, fit_func = fit_funcs, m_cal_simple
)
all(r -> r.gof.converged, values(result_fit)) || error("A peak fit did not converge")
true

Each entry holds the fitted parameters with uncertainties, for example the position (centroid) and the width (fwhm) of the 2614.5 keV peak:

result_fit[:Tl208FEP].centroid, result_fit[:Tl208FEP].fwhm
(261918.2 ± 1.1, 294.72 ± 0.85)
lplot(report_fit, figsize = (600, 400 * length(report_fit)), title = "Peak Fits", watermark = false)

Fitting the Calibration Curve

fit_calibration fits a polynomial that maps the fitted peak positions in ADC units to the literature energies. The escape peaks are excluded, because their positions are not tied to a line of the source in the same way. The polynomial order cal_pol_order = 1 gives a linear function. e_expression is the expression of the uncalibrated energy that appears in the function string of the result.

cal_names = [p for p in th228_names if p ∉ excluded_peaks]
result_calib, report_calib = fit_calibration(
    cal_pol_order,
    [result_fit[p].centroid for p in cal_names],
    [th228_lines_dict[p] for p in cal_names];
    e_expression = "e_uncal + $(only(result_ctc.fct)) * qdrift"
)
result_calib.gof.converged || error("The calibration curve fit did not converge")
result_calib.par
2-element Vector{Unitful.Quantity{Measurements.Measurement{Float64}, 𝐋^2 𝐌 𝐓^-2, Unitful.FreeUnits{(keV,), 𝐋^2 𝐌 𝐓^-2, nothing}}}:
      -4.72 ± 0.014 keV
 0.01000018 ± 7.8e-8 keV

The function string of the result converts the uncalibrated energy and qdrift of a table directly to keV.

result_calib.func
"-4.720496254220661keV .* (e_uncal + 0.47616996718483623 * qdrift).^0 .+ 0.010000180298372758keV .* (e_uncal + 0.47616996718483623 * qdrift).^1"

The escape peaks are shown as additional points. They are not part of the fit.

lplot(
    report_calib, xerrscaling = 100, title = "Calibration Curve", watermark = false,
    additional_pts = (
        μ = [result_fit[p].centroid for p in excluded_peaks],
        peaks = [th228_lines_dict[p] for p in excluded_peaks]
    )
)

Fitting the Resolution Curve

The width of the peaks as a function of energy follows the square root of a polynomial in energy. fit_fwhm fits it to the widths of the peaks in keV. The fitted widths are in ADC units, so they are converted to keV with the calibration curve. The constant term of the calibration curve is subtracted, because a width is a difference of energies.

f_cal_widths(x) = report_calib.f_fit(x) .* report_calib.e_unit .- first(report_calib.par)
fwhm_names = [p for p in th228_names if p ∉ excluded_peaks]

result_fwhm, report_fwhm = fit_fwhm(
    fwhm_pol_order,
    [th228_lines_dict[p] for p in fwhm_names],
    f_cal_widths.([result_fit[p].fwhm for p in fwhm_names]);
    e_type_cal = :e_cal, uncertainty = true
)
result_fwhm.gof.converged || error("The resolution curve fit did not converge")
true

The result contains the parameters of the curve and its value at Qββ = 2039.06 keV, the Q-value of the neutrinoless double-beta decay of Ge-76.

result_fwhm.qbb
2.6599 ± 0.0068 keV

The curve is expressed in the calibrated energy e_cal:

result_fwhm.func_cal
"sqrt(1.3657944092745016 * e_cal^0 * keV^2 + 0.0027998485107786682 * e_cal^1 * keV^1)"
lplot(
    report_fwhm, title = "Resolution Curve", watermark = false,
    additional_pts = (
        peaks = [th228_lines_dict[p] for p in excluded_peaks],
        fwhm = f_cal_widths.([result_fit[p].fwhm for p in excluded_peaks])
    )
)

Calibrated Spectrum

The function string result_calib.func converts the uncalibrated energy and qdrift to keV. In the production dataflow, ljl_propfunc from LegendDataManagement evaluates such strings on a table of DSP outputs. Here the string is turned into a function directly.

calibrate = Core.eval(@__MODULE__, Meta.parse("(e_uncal, qdrift) -> " * result_calib.func))
e_cal = ustrip.(u"keV", Base.invokelatest.(calibrate, e_uncal, qdrift))

fig = Figure(size = (700, 400))
ax = Axis(
    fig[1, 1], xlabel = "Energy (keV)", ylabel = "Counts / 1 keV", yscale = log10,
    limits = ((0, 3000), (1, 2e4)), xticks = 0:500:3000, title = "Calibrated Spectrum"
)
stephist!(ax, e_cal, bins = 0:1:3000)
vlines!(ax, ustrip.(u"keV", th228_lines), color = (:red, 0.3), linestyle = :dash, label = "Literature energies")
axislegend(ax, position = :rt)
fig
